extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, regulators (EPA/CARB), automaker executives, state attorneys general, and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Preliminary, unedited transcript of a House Energy & Commerce Subcommittee hearing investigating Volkswagen's emissions defeat device allegations, documenting questions, procedural norms, regulatory expectations, and remedial/enforcement issues. Useful as a record of oversight criteria and enforcement-related requirements discussed by members and witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony under oath
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee takes testimony under oath and witnesses are sworn in; false statements are subject to penalties under Title 18, Section 1011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnesses are asked if they object to testifying under oath; after being sworn they are reminded of criminal penalties for false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel during testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Under House and committee rules, a witness is entitled to be advised by counsel during testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee asks witnesses whether they desire counsel before administering the oath; witnesses may decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation and document production
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee expects Volkswagen (and other parties) to cooperate with the inquiry by providing documents and information to the committee as quickly as possible, including documents already discussed publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members explicitly request rapid production of documents (including Board meeting materials) and note the committee will ask for additional follow-up questions with a 10-day response expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and clear, consistent communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Volkswagen must demonstrate transparency, cooperation, and clear, consistent communication with the committee, EPA, investigators, customers, suppliers, dealers, and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated exhortations that restoring public trust requires openness and consistent messaging; lack of transparency is criticized as prolonging uncertainty for consumers and dealers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and approval of Auxiliary Emissions Control Devices (AECD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Software features that affect emissions should be disclosed to and approved by regulators as an Auxiliary Emissions Control Device (AECD) in connection with the certification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Horn stated the emissions control strategy included a software feature that should have been disclosed/approved as an AECD; failure to do so is a central allegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification withdrawal when noncompliance suspected
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacturer should withdraw certification applications if unresolved emissions compliance issues are discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volkswagen withdrew its application for certification for all model year 2016 vehicles to show it acted immediately and to work with agencies on certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing methodology: dyno cycles + off-cycle + real-world monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's testing to detect defeat devices will combine the current five lab cycles, off-cycle dynamometer (dyno) testing, and real-world onboard monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency stated it is using a combination of these methods and will keep procedures unpredictable to avoid allowing automakers to game tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpredictability of testing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators should avoid sharing testing procedures with automakers to remain unpredictable and prevent gaming of certification tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explicitly said it would be careful not to share details of new testing approaches with automakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory enforcement objective: 'make the environment whole'
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal goal of enforcement actions regarding excess emissions is to make the environment whole by mitigating the environmental harm caused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA emphasized remediation/mitigation of excess tons of pollutants will factor into enforcement and resolution; financial/other penalties will be determined by ongoing investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer liability for excess emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Liability and responsibility for excess emissions rests with the manufacturer (Volkswagen) rather than vehicle owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA stated the responsibility and the liability for the excess emissions lies with Volkswagen, and the company will be responsible for fixes and mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumers should not be penalized for manufacturer's deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Vehicle owners who were deceived by the manufacturer should not be held responsible or penalized for emissions violations caused by defeat devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members and EPA noted owners are 'innocent' and consumer protection/compensation will be central to reviewing options; other federal and state consumer protection agencies have roles here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall orders and obligation to fix vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a remedy is validated and regulators are confident it is effective, authorities will order recalls and it will be the company's responsibility to fix affected vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA/CARB will require recalls after remedies are tested and validated; company must implement fixes and bear the cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy must preserve vehicle performance and fuel economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fix required by regulators should not negatively affect vehicle performance or fuel economy without clear disclosure and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members repeatedly asked whether fixes will affect performance/fuel economy and expect clear answers about tradeoffs before approving remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of remediation and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected consumers and dealers need timely information about how and when vehicles will be fixed and what to expect in the interim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members criticized vague timelines and demanded prompt answers about when fixes will be available and how consumers will be made whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability: identify responsible parties and potential criminal exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations should identify responsible individuals and entities; accountability could include steep fines and criminal prosecution under relevant statutes (e.g., TREAD Act referenced regarding enforcement tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee emphasized holding 'responsible parties' accountable and referenced prior oversight matters where individuals/companies faced serious consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify excess emissions and plan mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators and investigators must quantify the excess tons of pollutants emitted and develop a mitigation plan to address environmental/public health impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA acknowledged they know per-vehicle excess levels (10–40x) but must complete calculations and mitigation strategies to 'make the environment whole.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic accounting of affected vehicles for public-health assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide state-by-state (or jurisdictional) breakdowns of where affected vehicles are registered/reside to assess environmental and public-health impacts in specific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members requested state-level breakdowns to evaluate clusters and potential links to localized public-health issues; EPA/agency staff agreed to assist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with state authorities and respect for state enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should coordinate with state attorneys general and state environmental agencies; state laws (e.g., anti-tampering, fines, criminal penalties) remain relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnesses noted communication with state air directors and AGs; committee asked for compilation of state anti-tampering laws, fines, and criminal penalties as part of investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of regulatory resources and proactive testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators should have sufficient resources to perform real-world testing proactively rather than relying on third-party NGOs to identify noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: West Virginia University's (ICCT-funded) work triggered discovery; witnesses and members noted EPA needs resources for real-world testing to detect such issues earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative scope and candor about preliminary findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal and external investigations must be thorough and worldwide in scope; early-stage findings should be characterized as preliminary and shared when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Horn stated worldwide investigations have begun and that preliminary results will be shared as they are developed; committee asked for cooperation while investigators complete work.
